_sample_entry.title: Avoid SELECT * in large table queries
_sample_entry.problem_description: Using SELECT * retrieves all columns from a table, causing unnecessary I/O, memory consumption, and preventing columnar storage optimizations.
_sample_entry.root_cause: Developer convenience; schema not fully known at query-writing time; lack of query review process.
_sample_entry.optimization_strategy: Replace SELECT * with an explicit list of only the columns required by the downstream consumer or transformation.
_sample_entry.after_example: SELECT order_id, customer_id, status, created_at FROM orders WHERE status = 'active';
_sample_entry.explanation: Columnar storage engines (Spark, BigQuery, Hive ORC) read only the columns requested. Specifying columns explicitly enables column pruning, reduces bytes scanned, lowers memory pressure on executors, and decreases shuffle costs in distributed environments.

expected_impact.cost: Medium reduction in cloud scan costs
expected_impact.memory: Proportional reduction based on columns eliminated

_sample_entry.source: AWS Data Engineering Best Practices Guide
_sample_entry.embedding_text: Avoid SELECT * in large table queries. SELECT * retrieves all columns causing unnecessary I/O and memory usage. Replace SELECT * with explicit column list. SELECT * column pruning I/O optimization query rewrite columnar storage.
_sample_entry.notes: Less impactful on narrow tables (< 5 columns) or row-store engines for point lookups.
